text:
andrew: quick design question. we keep running into ENI/IP pressure when onboarding lots of small customers with PrivateLink. has anyone explored a 'regional relay' pattern instead of per-customer interface endpoints?
mira: interesting. can you sketch the pattern?
andrew: idea: customer still gets private connectivity but instead of each customer creating an interface endpoint to our account, we deploy a tiny relay (NLB + autoscaling group or small EKS) inside a customer-managed subnet or in a delegated customer account. many customers would connect to one relay instance per region. relay then proxies to our control plane over a small number of shared ENIs.
sam: so basically move the per-customer ENI count into a per-region relay inside the customer boundary. that reduces ENI explosion in our accounts but increases infra we ask customers to run.
devin: variants:
- relay-in-customer: customer deploys our lightweight relay AMI/container. they keep NZ ownership of ENIs; we get fewer interface endpoints on our side.
- relay-managed: we deploy a regional relay in our account but customers peer to it/TGW. that still creates routes per-customer and may reintroduce scale issues.
- multi-tenant PrivateLink aggregator: customer creates interface endpoints to a small set of aggregator services we run (per-region), and aggregator maps to customer context at L7.
mira: aggregator sounds promising but how do we preserve isolation and attribution? billing needs per-customer bytes and logs.
sam: we can require customers to include a header or mTLS client cert per-connection so aggregator can tag metrics. or the relay in their account is simpler: it's already customer-isolated; we just accept authenticated traffic from it.
andrew: some pros/cons I noted:
- relay-in-customer pros: avoids ENI/IP limits in our account, preserves network isolation, allows local KMS/HSM usage for crypto if needed. cons: onboarding friction, support surface, life-cycle ops in customer account.
- aggregator pros: simpler for customers (just create endpoint), less infra to run across thousands of accounts. cons: we need per-customer tagging, harder to guarantee no noisy neighbor CPU/latency, potential compliance issues.
devin: also DNS & discovery differences. PrivateLink with private DNS gives a nice transparent host name. with relays we rely on customers configuring DNS or passing relay IPs to us. we can automate via CloudFormation stacks that set up private hosted zones and resolver rules.
nate: another option is reuse of Route53 resolver inbound endpoints. customer creates an inbound resolver endpoint and we do DNS-based routing to a shared endpointset. but that doesn't solve ENI counts entirely and inbound resolver has its own quotas.
mira: auth model? we should insist on mTLS from relay -> control plane and mutual auth at L7. if relay runs in customer account it can hold customer keys and do local KMS operations.
sam: cost model: per-GB PrivateLink fees add up. relay-in-customer uses customer's network egress inside VPC so the customer eats intra-region data transfer; for us aggregator has per-GB costs on our side. need to simulate both for 10k customers with median 50MB/day.
andrew: edge cases: customers with /28 subnets or very small CIDRs won't have spare IPs for ENIs. relay pattern sidesteps that since relay lives in larger subnet or is customer-managed so they can choose placement.
devin: implementation notes for relay-in-customer (rough):
1) publish CFN module that creates: security group (443 only), autoscaling EKS profile or ASG, IAM role, CloudWatch metrics, optional Route53 private zone entries.
2) customer runs stack in their account; stack registers relay with our control plane via a bootstrap token.
3) relay establishes mTLS to control plane and accepts inbound PrivateLink/interface endpoint traffic locally.

example bootstrap flow (very rough):
```
# customer runs our cloudformation and gets a registration token
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.test/register-relay -d '{ token: "abc" }'
# relay then performs mutual TLS handshake to control plane and announces region/capacity
```
mira: operations: we need auto-rotation for certs, automatic upgrades for relay images, and telemetry shipped back to console. also clear kill-switch if customer asks us to stop.
sam: monitoring: per-relay metrics (conn count, bytes, error rate), and per-customer attribution tags. alerts when relay health degrades or when IPs in customer's subnet drop below threshold.
andrew: compliance: for customers who need to keep keys local, relay can do decryption locally and only send envelopes back. helps with KMS/HSM constraints.
nate: security: make sure the relay's SG only accepts the interface endpoint subnets and port 443; limit IAM roles of relay to minimal scope.
devin: we should prototype both: CFN relay stack + aggregator prototype using NLB+target groups and a light L7 mapper. measure ENI counts, latency added, and ops overhead.
infra-bot: task created INFRA-2719: prototype customer-side relay CFN + aggregator NLB in staging. assign: devin (aggregator), sam (cost sim), andrew (relay CFN), mira (onboarding doc)
mira: action items from this thread:
- andrew: draft a short doc comparing three patterns (per-customer PrivateLink, relay-in-customer, aggregator) with costs, ops, and security notes (due Fri)
- devin: spin up aggregator NLB prototype in staging and record ENI usage and latency (2 weeks)
- sam: run cost/IP simulation for 1k/10k customers with median token sizes (next Tues)
- mira: create onboarding checklist for relay stack and required DNS steps

andrew: thanks. if anyone has strong objections to relay pattern speak now. otherwise i'll start the doc and attach diagrams. :thumbsup:
